{{Short description|Mathematician, cybersecurity expert and advocate for gender equality}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Asha Rao''' is a mathematician and expert in cyber security. She is the Associate Dean, or Head of Department, of Mathematical Sciences and Professor at [[RMIT University]].

== Education and career ==
Rao completed her PhD in Algebra at the [[University of Pune]]. She started working at [[RMIT University]] as a lecturer in 1992, and became a Professor in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Asha Rao |url=https://scienceandtechnologyaustralia.org.au/profile/asha-rao/ |access-date=2023-10-11 |website=Science and Technology Australia |language=en-AU}}</ref>

Her higher education teaching and curriculum design in mathematics and cybersecurity, as well as her trans-disciplinary research expertise applying mathematics have been used to solve real world problems for a range of industry partners including the Department of Defence. Professor Rao is the Founding Chair of Women In Mathematics<ref>{{Cite web |title=WIMSIG NEWSLETTER — February 2014 |url=https://austms.org.au/special-interest-groups/wimsig/wimsig-news/wimsig-newsletter-february-2014-2/ |access-date=2022-04-07 |website=Australian Mathematical Society |language=en-US}}</ref> and her leadership and advocacy for women in STEM has been recognised by the award of RMIT STEM [[Athena SWAN|Athena Swan]] Award.

One facet of her research focuses on the mathematical foundations of quantum cryptography, coding theory, and risk management. This involves utilizing algebraic methods in the realms of communication, coding, and information theory, as well as employing risk management strategies to ensure adherence to regulations, such as the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Terrorism Act.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-07-30 |title=Asha Rao |url=https://theconversation.com/profiles/asha-rao-133224 |access-date=2023-10-11 |website=The Conversation |language=en}}</ref>

Rao has authored more than 60 refereed scientific publications and contributed chapters to two scholarly books.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asha Rao |url=https://scholar.google.com.au/citations?user=SluqKR0AAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2022-04-07 |website=scholar.google.com.au}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |title=Algebraic design theory and Hadamard matrices : ADTHM, Lethbridge, Alberta, Canada, July 2014 |date=2015 |others=C. J. Colbourn |isbn=978-3-319-17729-8 |location=Cham |oclc=920465940}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Burry |first=Jane |title=Designing the dynamic |date=2013 |publisher=Melbourne Books |isbn=978-1-922129-13-0 |location=Melbourne |oclc=822348582}}</ref>

== Media ==
Highlights include influential academic contributions in the cyber security space<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tam |first1=Tracy |last2=Rao |first2=Asha |last3=Hall |first3=Joanne |date=2021-12-29 |title=The Invisible COVID-19 Small Business Risks: Dealing with the Cyber-Security Aftermath |journal=Digital Government: Research and Practice |volume=2 |issue=2 |pages=23:1–23:8 |doi=10.1145/3436807 |issn=2691-199X|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title=The Good, The Bad and The Missing: A Narrative Review of Cyber-security Implications for Australian Small Businesses |journal=Computers & Security|year=2021 |doi=10.1016/j.cose.2021.102385 |arxiv=2109.00733 |last1=Tam |first1=Tracy |last2=Rao |first2=Asha |last3=Hall |first3=Joanne |volume=109 |article-number=102385 |s2cid=237386633 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=2021 |title=Rapid Cybersecurity Assessment System for Small Business' COVID Move to Online |url=https://www.ndss-symposium.org/wp-content/uploads/coronadef2021_23004_paper.pdf |journal=Workshop on Secure IT Technologies Against COVID-19 (CoronaDef) 2021, NDSS Symposium}}</ref> as well as science communication outreach advocating for the importance of mathematics in high profile media platforms such as the ''[[Australian Financial Review]]''<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-12-06 |title=Calculus ignored even though evidence is we rely on it |url=https://www.afr.com/work-and-careers/education/calculus-ignored-even-though-evidence-is-we-rely-on-it-20201204-p56ksf |access-date=2022-04-07 |website=Australian Financial Review |language=en}}</ref> and ''[[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]]''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Rao |first=Asha |title=A forced PIN for all credit cards won't stop the biggest fraud |url=http://theconversation.com/a-forced-pin-for-all-credit-cards-wont-stop-the-biggest-fraud-29898 |access-date=2022-04-07 |website=The Conversation |date=31 July 2014 |language=en}}</ref>

Rao has published on the use of signatures, PINs and credit card fraud in 2014, for The Conversation.<ref name=":0" /> Rao has contributed to numerous podcasts, discussing cybersecurity, mathematics and physics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-14 |title=Asha Rao – Top podcast episodes |url=https://www.listennotes.com/top-podcasts/asha-rao/ |access-date=2023-10-11 |website=Listen Notes |language=en}}</ref>

Rao has been interviewed by SAARI for National Science Week,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-08-21 |title=Powerhouse South Asian Women in STEM - In Conversations with Dr Asha Rao and Dr Astha Singh - SAARI Collective |url=https://saaricollective.com.au/community/blog/powerhouse-south-asian-women-in-stem-in-conversations-with-dr-asha-rao-and-dr-astha-singh/ |access-date=2024-07-24 |language=en-US}}</ref> Women’s Agenda,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tu |first=Jessie |date=2020-02-11 |title=Four women in science share career tips on International Day of Women and Girls in Science |url=https://womensagenda.com.au/leadership/four-women-in-science-share-career-tips-on-international-day-of-women-and-girls-in-science/ |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=Women's Agenda |language=en-AU}}</ref> ACEMS,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Episode 44: Overcoming Imposter Syndrome {{!}} ARC Centre of Excellence for Mathematical and Statistical Frontiers |url=https://acems.org.au/podcast/episode-44-overcoming-imposter-syndrome |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=acems.org.au}}</ref> and provided expert commentary on cybercrime in the ABC News.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2020-09-18 |title=If it happened to Tony Abbott, it could happen to you: the simple mistakes that could bring you undone online |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-09-19/tony-abbott-boarding-pass-online-cyber-safety-mistake/12678776 |access-date=2024-07-24 |work=ABC News |language=en-AU}}</ref> 

During the latter part of 2020, she undertook the position of Interim Director at the Australian Mathematical Sciences Institute (AMSI) while concurrently holding the position of Associate Dean. AMSI serves as the collaborative effort of 14 Australian universities and serves as the leading organization advocating for mathematics in Australia.<ref name="professor_asha_rao">{{Cite web |date=2021-11-13 |title=Professor Asha Rao |url=https://www.vic.gov.au/professor-asha-rao |access-date=2023-10-11 |website=www.vic.gov.au |language=en-AU}}</ref>

== Gender ==
Rao has worked to address gender-related challenges that hinder the advancement of women and girls in STEM professions. In her role as the inaugural leader of Women in Maths, she has spearheaded various programs aimed at enhancing gender equality in the field of mathematical sciences in Australia. She remains an advocate for encouraging young women to pursue mathematics, actively engaging in discussions about this imperative through both conventional media and social platforms.<ref name="professor_asha_rao" />

== Awards and recognition ==
Rao has been recognised by numerous awards including:

2021 Australia India Science, Research & Development Award, India and Australia Business and Community Alliance<ref>{{Cite web |title=IABCA Alumni |url=https://www.iabca.com.au/alumni |access-date=2022-04-07 |website=iabca |language=en}}</ref>

2021 [[Victorian Honour Roll of Women]] Trailblazer<ref>{{Cite web |title=Victorian Government Honour Roll of women inductees |url=https://www.vic.gov.au/professor-asha-rao}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-11-18 |title=AMSI Congratulates Professor Asha Rao on Induction to Victorian Honour Roll of Women |url=https://amsi.org.au/2021/11/18/amsi-congratulates-professor-asha-rao/ |access-date=2022-04-07 |website=AMSI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Indian-Australian Trailblazer Mathematician Prof. Asha Rao Inducted to Victorian Honour Roll of Women – Australia Today |date=24 November 2021 |url=https://www.theaustraliatoday.com.au/indian-australian-trailblazer-mathematician-prof-asha-rao-inducted-to-victorian-honour-roll-of-women/ |access-date=2022-04-07 |language=en-AU}}</ref>

2019 [[Superstars of STEM]], Science and Technology Australia<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Asha Rao |url=https://scienceandtechnologyaustralia.org.au/profile/asha-rao/ |access-date=2022-04-07 |website=Science and Technology Australia |language=en-AU}}</ref>

2016 RMIT Media Stars Award
